key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection to reduce weld defects, thermal gradients and axial-force fluctuations in HDPE joining.
method: Model heat, forces, material flow and void formation using a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian simulation.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Combine predictions to map defective and defect-free welding windows.
evidence_signal: Simulations agreed with experiments, neural networks achieved R² of 0.91–0.99, and 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Prediction accuracy outside the tested process-parameter space remains unestablished.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
